content: The Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center El Paso Campus is a branch of the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center (TTUHSC) located in El Paso, Texas. It was originally established in 1969 as the Regional Academic Health Center. In 1973, it became affiliated with R.E. Thomason Hospital as part of the TTUHSC system. Currently, the campus employs approximately 1,200 faculty and staff members. Medical education at this campus includes training for thirdand fourth-year medical students, as well as residents enrolled in eight accredited residency programs. The El Paso campus operates eleven community clinics distributed throughout the city and county of El Paso. It maintains partnerships with several healthcare institutions, including R.E. Thomason Hospital, William Beaumont Army Medical Center at Fort Bliss, and Providence Hospital. The campus is undergoing significant expansion, with three new buildings under construction and one building already completed in preparation for the opening of a full four-year medical school, projected for 2009. This medical school will be the first four-year medical school located on the U.S.-Mexico border. It is anticipated to have a substantial economic impact on the region, contributing an estimated $1.31 billion to the local economy by 2013. The El Paso campus is uniquely positioned to address healthcare issues specific to the border and Hispanic populations. It aims to lead research efforts that will significantly influence national healthcare literature, particularly in areas such as diabetes, obesity, and depression, which are prevalent in the El Paso region. In 2005, the campus initiated the Infinity Campaign, a fundraising effort to secure $25 million in private donations to support the construction of the four-year medical school. On August 4, 2007, Paul Foster, the President and CEO of Western Refining, made a historic $50 million donation to the school. This contribution represents the largest single donation in the history of the Texas Tech University System.
